```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
options(knitr.kable.NA = '')
```

## Background

Quick comparison of selected analytes measured during SuRGE, the two most recent NLA campaigns (NLA17 and NLA22), lagos, and aquamatch (doc and chla).

## Data

Required data are created via the targets pipeline. Load data here.

```{r data, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
tar_load(dat_raw)
tar_load(lagos_chem)
tar_load(aquamatch_data)
dat_lagos <- left_join(lagos_chem, dat_raw, relationship = "many-to-many")
dat_aquamatch <- left_join(aquamatch_data, dat_raw, by = "lake_id", relationship = "many-to-many")
```


## Extraction based chlorophyll a
We are missing extraction-based chlorophyll a measurements for `r dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(chla_lab_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` SuRGE lakes (mostly 2016 lakes). `r dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(chla_lab_shallow) & (!is.na(nla17_chla) | !is.na(nla22_chla)) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` of these lakes have chla estimates from 2017 and/or 2022 NLA. `r dat_lagos %>% filter(is.na(chla_lab_shallow) & (!is.na(lagos_chla_shallow)) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` of these lakes have chla estimates from LAGOS, and `r dat_aquamatch %>% filter(is.na(chla_lab_shallow) & (!is.na(aquamatch_chla_shallow)) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` lakes has chla from aquamatch.

As expected, the concurrence among the various datasets is not great. 

The LAGOS and aquamatch data highlight the temporal variation within a lake ( time series available for most lakes, hover cursor over point to reveal sample date). Matching values by sample data is likely important. 



```{r chla_plot, echo=FALSE}

{dat_raw %>%
    select(lake_id, nla17_site_id, nla22_site_id,
           chla_lab_shallow, nla17_chla, nla22_chla) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = c(nla17_chla, nla22_chla),
      names_to = "nla_year",
      values_to = "nla_chla"
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(nla_chla), !is.na(chla_lab_shallow)) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = c(nla17_site_id, nla22_site_id),
      names_to = "nla_parameter",
      values_to = "nla_site_id"
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(nla_site_id)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(
      nla_chla, chla_lab_shallow, 
      text = paste("SuRGE:", chla_lab_shallow, "<br>",
                   "NLA:", nla_chla, "<br>",
                   "nla_site_id:", nla_site_id, "<br>",
                   "SuRGE lake_id:", lake_id),
      color = nla_year
    )
    ) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    ggtitle("Extraction Based Chlorophyll a") +
    xlab("NLA chla") +
    ylab("SuRGE chla")} %>%
  ggplotly(tooltip = "text")


{dat_lagos %>%
    select(lake_id, lagoslakeid, sample_date,
           chla_lab_shallow, lagos_chla_shallow) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    filter(!is.na(lagos_chla_shallow)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(
      lagos_chla_shallow, chla_lab_shallow, 
      text = paste("SuRGE:", chla_lab_shallow, "<br>",
                   "LAGOS:", lagos_chla_shallow, "<br>",
                   "lagoslakeid:", lagoslakeid, "<br>",
                   "SuRGE lake_id:", lake_id, "<br>",
                   "LAGOS sample date:", sample_date),
      color = as.factor(lake_id)
    )
    ) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    ggtitle("Extraction Based Chlorophyll a") +
    xlab("LAGOS chla") +
    ylab("SuRGE chla")} %>%
  ggplotly(tooltip = "text")


{dat_aquamatch %>%
    select(lake_id, activity_start_date,
           chla_lab_shallow, aquamatch_chla_shallow) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    filter(!is.na(aquamatch_chla_shallow)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(
      aquamatch_chla_shallow, chla_lab_shallow, 
      text = paste("SuRGE:", chla_lab_shallow, "<br>",
                   "aquamatch:", aquamatch_chla_shallow, "<br>",
                   "SuRGE lake_id:", lake_id, "<br>",
                   "aquamatch sample date:", activity_start_date),
      color = as.factor(lake_id)
    )
    ) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    ggtitle("Extraction Based Chlorophyll a") +
    xlab("aquamatch chla") +
    ylab("SuRGE chla")} %>%
  ggplotly(tooltip = "text")
```


None of the datasets have chla from the same year as the SuRGE sampling.  

Are there other data sources we can mine? See here for some 2013-2014 data (https://dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/epa.ohio.gov/Portals/35/tmdl/2016IR.pdf). Scott Jacobs will dig into USACE data. I found data for Acton Lake (lake_id == 1001) from Vanni's EDI repo.



```{r chla_table, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
left_join(
  dat_raw %>% 
    select(lake_id, visit, sample_start, 
           chla_lab_shallow, nla17_chla, nla22_chla) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    filter(
      is.na(chla_lab_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)
    ) %>%
    select(-visit),
  dat_lagos %>% 
    select(lake_id, sample_date, lagos_chla_shallow) %>%
    rename(lagos_sample_date = sample_date)
) %>%
  left_join(
    dat_aquamatch %>%
      filter(!is.na(aquamatch_chla_shallow)) %>%
      select(lake_id, activity_start_date, aquamatch_chla_shallow) %>%
      rename(aquamatch_sample_date = activity_start_date) %>%
      distinct()
  ) %>%
  rename(surge_sample_date = sample_start) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(lagos_chla_shallow) | 
      !is.na(aquamatch_chla_shallow) | 
      !is.na(nla17_chla) | 
      !is.na(nla22_chla)
  ) %>%
  select(-chla_lab_shallow) %>%
  arrange(lake_id, aquamatch_sample_date) %>% 
  distinct() %>%
  kableExtra::kable(caption = "Table 3. NLA, LAGOS, and aquamatch chla data for missing lakes") %>% 
  column_spec(1, bold = T) %>%
  kable_styling("hover", full_width = FALSE) %>%
  collapse_rows(columns = 1:2)

```

## SO4
Sulfate wasn't measured until 2021 and we are missing data for `r dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(so4_shallow)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` SuRGE lakes. `r dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(so4_shallow) & (!is.na(nla17_sulfate) | !is.na(nla22_sulfate))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` of these lakes have sulfate estimates from 2017 and/or 2022 NLA and `r dat_lagos %>% filter(is.na(so4_shallow) & (!is.na(lagos_so4_shallow))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` of these lakes have sulfate estimates from LAGOS. 


Comparison of SuRGE and NLA sulfate measurements is actually pretty good. Interestingly, most of the outliers in the plot below are in New Mexico South Dakota. I double checked the NLA and SuRGE data for these sites and don't see any issues. The New Mexico data shown are the mean of visits 1 and 2, which had very similar results. NLA sampled NLA22_NM-10013 in 2017 and 2022 with very similar results (data shown, 243 vs 83). 

Comparison with LAGOS is also pretty good. Again, the time series is useful for visualizing temporal variation.



```{r so4_plot, echo=FALSE}
{
  dat_raw %>%
    select(
      lake_id, nla17_site_id, nla22_site_id,
      so4_shallow, nla17_sulfate, nla22_sulfate
    ) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = c(nla17_sulfate, nla22_sulfate),
      names_to = "nla_year",
      values_to = "nla_so4"
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(nla_so4), !is.na(so4_shallow)) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = c(nla17_site_id, nla22_site_id),
      names_to = "nla_parameter",
      values_to = "nla_site_id"
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(nla_site_id)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(
      nla_so4, so4_shallow,
      text = paste(
        "SuRGE:", so4_shallow, "<br>",
        "NLA:", nla_so4, "<br>",
        "nla_site_id:", nla_site_id, "<br>",
        "SuRGE lake_id:", lake_id
      ),
      color = nla_year
    )) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    ggtitle("Sulfate") +
    xlab("NLA SO4") +
    ylab("SuRGE SO4")
} %>%
  ggplotly(tooltip = "text")


{dat_lagos %>%
    select(lake_id, lagoslakeid, sample_date,
           so4_shallow, lagos_so4_shallow) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    filter(!is.na(lagos_so4_shallow)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(
      lagos_so4_shallow, so4_shallow, 
      text = paste("SuRGE:", so4_shallow, "<br>",
                   "LAGOS:", lagos_so4_shallow, "<br>",
                   "lagoslakeid:", lagoslakeid, "<br>",
                   "SuRGE lake_id:", lake_id, "<br>",
                   "LAGOS sample date:", sample_date),
      color = as.factor(lake_id)
    )
    ) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    ggtitle("Sulfate") +
    xlab("LAGOS SO4") +
    ylab("SuRGE SO4")} %>%
  ggplotly(tooltip = "text")
```

The table shows the available data for the missing observations. A few lakes have observations over multiple years and these show pretty good agreement. I think we can impute the missing SO4 using NLA and LAGOS, but that still leaves 31 lakes with no data. We may need to dig a bit for lake-specific data reports.



```{r so4_table, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
full_join(
  dat_raw %>% 
    filter(
      is.na(so4_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1) & (!is.na(nla17_sulfate) | !is.na(nla22_sulfate))
      ) %>% 
    distinct(
      lake_id, sample_start, nla17_sulfate, nla22_sulfate
      ) %>% 
    rename(
      SuRGE_sample_date = sample_start, 
      NLA17_SO4 = nla17_sulfate, 
      NLA22_SO4 = nla22_sulfate
      ), 
  dat_lagos %>% 
    filter(
      is.na(so4_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1) & !is.na(lagos_so4_shallow)
      ) %>% 
    select(
      lake_id, sample_start, sample_date, lagos_so4_shallow
      ) %>% 
    distinct() %>% 
    rename(
      SuRGE_sample_date = sample_start, 
      lagos_sample_date = sample_date)
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable(caption = "Table 3. NLA and LAGOS SO4 data for missing lakes") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

Another possibility is to estimate sulfate based on conductivity. The relationship is pretty good in Northern Appalachians, Northern Plains, and Upper Midwest. Northern Plains lake 75 (Freeman Lake) is an outlier with exceptionally high SO4 given the conductivity. This lake is known to be weird; for example, nitrate is 30 mg/l! 

We could estimate sulfate from conductivity for the 10 Northern Appalachian and 2 Upper Midwest lakes for which it is missing.
```{r so4_by_eco, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
dat_raw %>% 
  filter(is.na(so4_shallow)) %>% 
  distinct(lake_id, ag_eco9_nm) %>%
  {table(.$ag_eco9_nm)} %>%
    kableExtra::kable(caption = "Number of lakes with missing sulfate by ecoregion") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

```

```{r so4_cond_plot, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
{dat_raw %>%
    filter(!is.na(ag_eco9_nm)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(
      sp_cond_shallow, so4_shallow, 
      text = paste("SuRGE lake_id:", lake_id))) +
    geom_point() +
    facet_wrap(~ag_eco9_nm, scales = "free") +
    theme(panel.spacing.y = unit(1.5, "cm"))} %>% 
  ggplotly(tooltip = "text")
```

## TN
We are missing TN measurements for `r dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(tn_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` SuRGE lakes. NLA contains TN observations for `r if(dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(tn_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1) & (!is.na(nla17_ntl) | !is.na(nla22_ntl))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow() == 0) {print("none")} else {dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(tn_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1) & (!is.na(nla17_ntl) | !is.na(nla22_ntl))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()}` of these lakes. LAGOS contains TN for 
`r dat_lagos %>% filter(is.na(tn_shallow) & (!is.na(lagos_tn_shallow))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` of these lakes.

The NLA comparison with TN is pretty good. Also, the 2 lakes with NLA17 and NLA22 observations agree pretty well (Table 2). I think we can imput the missing SuRGE data with the NLA numbers, especially the 2 NLA22 lakes.

`r dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(tn_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1) & (!is.na(nla17_ntl) | !is.na(nla22_ntl))) %>% distinct(lake_id, sample_start, nla17_ntl, nla22_ntl) %>% rename(SuRGE_sample_date = sample_start, NLA17_TN = nla17_ntl, NLA22_TN = nla22_ntl) %>% kableExtra::kable(caption = "Table 2. NLA TN data for missing lakes") %>% kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)`

## DOC
We are missing DOC measurements for `r dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(doc_shallow) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` SuRGE lakes. NLA contains DOC observations for `r if(dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(doc_shallow) & (!is.na(nla17_doc) | !is.na(nla22_doc))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow() == 0) {print("none")} else {dat_raw %>% filter(is.na(doc_shallow) & (!is.na(nla17_doc) | !is.na(nla22_doc))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()}` of these lakes. LAGOS contains data for 
`r dat_lagos %>% filter(is.na(doc_shallow) & (!is.na(lagos_doc_shallow))) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` of these lakes. `r dat_aquamatch %>% filter(is.na(doc_shallow) & (!is.na(aquamatch_doc_shallow)) & !(lake_id %in% c(250, 281) & visit == 1)) %>% distinct(lake_id) %>% nrow()` lakes has DOC from aquamatch.

Pretty good concurence between NLA and SuRGE DOC, a bit weaker with LAGOS, but look at the data in table 3. Very good concurence between repeat measurements at one lake, even across multiple years. I think we can impute the missing DOC using NLA, LAGOS, and aquamatch. These 3 datasets provide matches to 51 of the missing lakes.

The only DOC data available for seven of the lakes are from aquamatch observations in the late 1970s. The 1970's data matches contemporay observations fairly well in a few of the other lakes (e.g. 1026, 1019, 1011) so maybe these old data are OK, but more recent observations would be preferable.

## Put it all together
The code below replaces missing values with those from NLA, LAGOS, or aquamatch. Preference is given to values from the same year as the SuRGE sampling, else we use the mean of all available data. Aquamatch values from earlier than 2009 are ommitted.


```{r impute, echo=FALSE, message = FALSE}
# TN
# missing values are from 2022 SuRGE sampling. Replace with
# NLA22 when available, else NLA17.
dat_raw <- 
  dat_raw %>%
  mutate(tn_shallow = case_when(
    is.na(tn_shallow) & !is.na(nla22_ntl) ~ nla22_ntl,
    is.na(tn_shallow) & is.na(nla22_ntl) & !is.na(nla17_ntl) ~ nla17_ntl,
    TRUE ~ tn_shallow
  ))

# chla
# only have data for Acton Lake (1001) from Vanni's EDI repo
# https://portal.edirepository.org/nis/mapbrowse?packageid=edi.256.3
# input_data/ActonLakeIntegrated.csv
dat_raw <- 
  dat_raw %>%
  mutate(chla_lab_shallow = case_when(
    lake_id == 1001 ~ 28.98, # 28.98 ug/L from Vanni for 5/31/2016
    TRUE ~ chla_lab_shallow
  ))

# SULFATE
# impute with lagos and/or NLA
# none of the lagos or NLA data are from same year at SuRGE
# observations, so just use mean
dat_raw <- left_join(
  # 1st df
  dat_raw,
  # bring in lagos data
  dat_lagos %>%
    select(
      lake_id, lagos_so4_shallow
    ) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    # exclude missing observations
    filter(!is.na(lagos_so4_shallow)) %>%
    # mean by lake
    group_by(lake_id) %>%
    summarize(lagos_so4_shallow = mean(lagos_so4_shallow))
) %>%
  # replace missing value with mean nla17, nla22, and lagos sulfate by lake.
  # this is a rowwise operation
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(
    so4_shallow = case_when(
      is.na(so4_shallow) ~ mean(
        c(nla17_sulfate, nla22_sulfate, lagos_so4_shallow),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ), # close mean
      TRUE ~ so4_shallow
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup %>% # remove rowwise
  select(-lagos_so4_shallow)
  

# DOC
dat_raw <- left_join(
  # 1st df
  dat_raw,
  # join aquamatch data!
  dat_aquamatch %>%
    select(lake_id, activity_start_date, aquamatch_doc_shallow) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    # exclude lake 83 values not wanted. Remaining values
    # are temporally matched (2020-07-27, 2020-08-28) to surge
    # sampling date (2020-08-10)
    filter(
      !(lake_id == 83 & 
          (activity_start_date <= as.Date("2020-06-25") | 
             activity_start_date >= as.Date("2020-09-23")))
    ) %>% # close filter
    # Omit observations from 1970s (all others are > 2009-01-01)
    filter(
      activity_start_date > as.Date("2009-01-01")
    ) %>%
    # calculate mean by lake (collapse time series into one value)
    group_by(lake_id) %>%
    summarize(
      aquamatch_doc_shallow = mean(aquamatch_doc_shallow, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(aquamatch_doc_shallow), !is.nan(aquamatch_doc_shallow))
) %>% # close left_join
  left_join(
    # join lagos data
    dat_lagos %>%
      select(
        lake_id, lagos_doc_shallow
      ) %>%
      distinct() %>%
      # exclude missing observations
      filter(!is.na(lagos_doc_shallow)) %>%
      # mean by lake
      group_by(lake_id) %>%
      summarize(lagos_doc_shallow = mean(lagos_doc_shallow))
  ) %>% # close second join 
    # replace missing value with mean nla17, nla22, lagos, and aquamatch
  # DOC by lake.
  # this is a rowwise operation
  rowwise() %>% 
mutate(
  doc_shallow = case_when(
    lake_id == 83 ~ aquamatch_doc_shallow, # sampling date match
    is.na(doc_shallow) ~ mean(
        c(nla17_doc, nla22_doc, lagos_doc_shallow, aquamatch_doc_shallow),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ), # close mean
      TRUE ~ so4_shallow
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup %>% # remove rowwise
  select(-lagos_doc_shallow, -aquamatch_doc_shallow)


```

## Modeled Sulfate
As shown in SO4 section, SO4 can be predicted from conductivity in the Northern Appalachians and Northern Plains ecoregions. This is implemented in R/impute_data.R

```{r so4_model, echo=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

# reload data with no imputed values
tar_load(dat_raw)

# This bit predicts missing SO4 for the two ecoregions.
# After predictions, these data need to replace those in dat_raw
# Also, data imputed from other sources (e.g. NLA) should be 
# done prior to predicting missing values.
so4_models <- dat_raw %>%
  filter(
    ag_eco9_nm %in% c("Northern Appalachians", "Upper Midwest")
  ) %>%
  group_by(ag_eco9_nm) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    model = map(data, ~ {
      # Apply lm to each nested tibble
      model <- lm(so4_shallow ~ sp_cond_shallow, data = .)
      
      # Predict missing values
      missing_rows <- is.na(.x$so4_shallow)
      if (any(missing_rows)) {
        .x$so4_shallow[missing_rows] <- predict(model, newdata = .x[missing_rows, ])
      }
      .x
    })
  ) %>%
  unnest(data)

```
